ParleyPort brings a kit along: one Go module for every app that pairs through it, and with it the fortress that puts all your apps under one phrase.

## ✨ Added

- **The kit for app authors.** `github.com/junkerderprovinz/parleyport/kit` is the client side of ParleyPort as a Go module of its own, with its own tags of the form `kit/vX.Y.Z`, starting at 1.0.0. It holds what every app used to keep a copy of: the twelve words, the member keys, the relay client, finding the other instances on the network and the group with its approvals.
- **Pairing by phrase alone.** Instances of one app pair with the twelve words and nothing else. On one network they find each other and talk directly, and from different networks they meet on a relay. Nobody has to type an address, ever.
- **The fortress.** One phrase joins every app of a household, and joining pairs each app with its own instances as well. Every action an app offers the others has its own switch. When the phrase changes, members that missed it follow on their own for 30 days, and the fortress shows which devices stayed behind. A newcomer still holding the old phrase finds nobody home.
- **Apps call only the actions they list.** An app has to name every action it calls at another app in its `Uses`, and that list is also where the action's switch comes from. A call to anything else is turned away with 403 `not_used`, and `Act` returns `ErrNotUsed`.
- **Status, events and rules.** Every app answers the same status report and log, and `statustest` lets an app prove that in its own tests. Apps keep their events in a ring the other members read, and rules let one app act on what happened in another.
- **Notifications to ten services.** Webhooks, Discord, Slack, Gotify, ntfy, Matrix, mail, Apprise, Healthchecks and Unraid's own notifications, all kept in one format. Secrets stay masked on every settings page, and an error never quotes one.
- **Home Assistant over MQTT.** `mqttha` announces an app as a device with the sensors and buttons it describes, found through Home Assistant's discovery.
- **One folder, seen from both sides.** `hostpath` turns a folder as a container sees it into the same folder on the host and back, so two apps in different containers can point each other at it.
- **Backups between apps.** A member can fetch another app's backup and hand it back later. The backup streams directly on the local network, checked piece by piece, and never takes the relay.
- **The fortress in an app's MCP server.** `fortressmcp` shows an assistant set up with one app the whole household: the members, their status and log, and the tools the other apps offer.
- **Two helpers for plugins without Go code.** Every release carries `fortress` and `notify` for linux/amd64 and arm64, with their checksums. `fortress` joins a fortress, lists the members, reads their status and asks one of them for an action. `notify` sends an event to the channels in a file and shows and saves those channels with every secret masked.
- **Runs on other Docker hosts.** `compose.yaml` starts the relay on any Linux server with Docker, and the README covers Synology, Proxmox and MOS. The download buttons link the compose file and the MOS Hub.
- **The relay logs when it starts refusing an address for failed handshakes.** A client turned away this way no longer looks like a relay that is down. The address itself stays out of the log.

## 🎨 Design

- **A new logo** on the banners and the icon.
- **The README draws its section headings as chapter bands**, and the download buttons fill each row before they start the next. The button generator describes ParleyPort without naming the apps it serves.

## ⚡ Improved

- **Bigger answers fit through the relay.** A frame may be 16 MiB, so an app can send answers of up to 8 MiB through it.
- **Large answers travel in parts of 1 MiB.** Each part tells the caller the answer is still coming, so a slow upload no longer runs out of time. A client or relay that doesn't know parts gets the answer in one piece, as before.
- **Time limits follow progress.** The relay writes a frame in small pieces, each with its own deadline, so a large frame on a slow line no longer gets cut off halfway.
- **ParleyPort names no app.** The startup banner, the README and the Docker Hub description call it a relay for apps that pair their instances. The protocol stays as it is, so every client connects exactly as before.
- **Newer base images.** The Go and Alpine images the container is built from are on their latest digests.

## 🐛 Fixed

- **The image is built with Go 1.27.4.** It closes two holes the relay could be reached through: a crafted request that could crash an HTTP/1 server (GO-2026-6859), and trust in compromised intermediate certificates (GO-2026-6809).
- **The default relay address in the code is parleyport.halleluja.design**, the name the apps dial. The old name relay.halleluja.design keeps answering.
